chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Three (things) were transmitted successively by the Prophets, from Adam (peace be upon him) until they reached the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When he would morning, he would say:

O Allah, I ask You for faith that accompanies my heart, and conviction until I know that nothing will befall me except what You have decreed for me, and make me pleased with what You have apportioned for me.

And some of our companions have narrated it and added to it: 'Until I do not love the hastening of what You have delayed, nor the delaying of what You have hastened. O Living, O Eternal! By Your mercy I cry for help. Rectify for me all my affairs, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, ever. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his family.'
ai.seo_question: What is the morning supplication of the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding faith and divine decree?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in Al-Kafi, highlights the continuity of prophetic tradition by tracing a specific morning supplication back to Adam, emphasizing its status as a timeless spiritual practice. It underscores key Shia theological concepts such as *al-Rida* (contentment with divine decree) and *al-Yaqin* (firm conviction), while the variant adds the profound plea for *Istighatha* (seeking help) through the name *Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum* to prevent spiritual negligence. This reflects the Shia emphasis on maintaining a constant, conscious connection with Allah throughout the day.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fazl Bin Abu Qurrat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Three (things) have come successively among the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, from Adam<sup>as</sup> until these arrived to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. Whenever it was morning, he<sup>saww</sup> was saying:

‘O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj for Eman to accompany mysaww heart with, and such conviction that Isaww would know that nothing would hit me except what has been Ordained for mesaww, and Cause mesaww to be pleased with whatever has been Apportioned for mesaww’’.

And some of our companions have reported, and there is an increase in it, ‘Until Isaww do not love the hastening of what has been Delayed, nor the delay of what has been Hastened with. O Living, O Eternal! By Yourazwj Mercy Isaww cry for Help. Correct for mesaww, myas affairs, all of it and do not Leave mesaww to myselfsaww even for the blink of an eye, ever, and Send Salawāts upon Muhammadsaww and hissaww Progenyasws’’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sharif ibn Sabiq from al-Fadl ibn abu Qurrah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“There are three things that the prophets inherited from Adam until they reached the Messenger of Allah. In the morning he would say, ‘O Lord, I request You to grant me a belief that accompany with my heart, a certainty in the fact that nothing can affect me except what You have written, make me happy with the share that You have assigned for me.’”
Certain individuals of our people have narrated the above Hadith with this addition:

“So I will not love hastening of what You have delayed, and the delay of what You have hastened, O Living, O Guardian, I plead for help through Your mercy, correct all of my affairs and do not leave me to my own soul not even for a blinking of an eye and grant al-Salat (favors) upon Muhammad and his family.”
